title: The Saturday Market Stall
story: Tomas set up his stall in the market square before the shops opened. He sold handmade cards and small jars of jam. His sister Rosa had painted the cards, and Tomas had written the prices on a board. He wore a green apron so people would know he worked there. At nine the first customers arrived. A woman bought two cards and paid with a large note. Tomas gave her the right change and thanked her. A boy knocked a crate of jam with his bag. Two jars rolled toward the path. Tomas caught one, and Rosa caught the other before it hit the stones. Nothing broke. The boy's mother said sorry and bought a jar to make up for the scare. After lunch a teacher ordered ten cards for her class. Rosa wrapped them in brown paper and tied the parcel with string. Tomas checked the coins in his tin and wrote the total in a small book. Near four o'clock the best cards were gone. He lowered the price of the last jars and called each one a bargain. An older man bought all three and said the jam smelled like summer. Tomas packed the empty crate and folded the cloth. Rosa counted the notes again while he took down the sign. They had sold more than last week. Tomas decided that a tidy stall would keep both the jam and the customers safe.

quiz.question: What did Tomas sell from the stall?
options: handmade cards and jars of jam
quiz.correctAnswer: handmade cards and jars of jam

quiz.question: Who caught the jar that Tomas did not catch?
quiz.explanation: She stopped it before it hit the stones.
quiz.supportingSentence: Tomas caught one, and Rosa caught the other before it hit the stones.

quiz.question: What did the teacher order after lunch?
quiz.explanation: Rosa wrapped that order in brown paper.

quiz.question: In this story, what does bargain mean?
quiz.explanation: He used the word when he reduced the last jars.
quiz.supportingSentence: He lowered the price of the last jars and called each one a bargain.

quiz.question: Why did Tomas want the stall to stay tidy?
options: so the jam and the customers would stay safe
so Rosa could paint during the sale
so the teacher would order soup
so the notes would look new
quiz.correctAnswer: so the jam and the customers would stay safe
quiz.explanation: He linked a tidy table with safety after the near accident.
quiz.supportingSentence: Tomas decided that a tidy stall would keep both the jam and the customers safe.
